2027-07-17.title: Saturday of the eighth week after Pentecost · St Alexius of Rome
readings: Thanks be to God, who spreads through us in every place the fragrance that comes from knowing Christ
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me”: good news to the poor, in the synagogue at Nazareth
2027-07-17.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost. Tomorrow is the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Alexius of Rome (റോമിലെ വി. അലക്സിയോസ്), keeps the anniversary of the episcopal ordination of Most Rev. Thomas Mar Koorilos (1997), and keeps the name day of Most Rev. Yoohanon Mar Alexios. The Panchangam gives the readings of the weekday only.
2027-07-17.verse: For we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing;
theo: Paul writes today from a worried heart. He has come to Troas to proclaim the good news, and the Lord has opened a door for him, yet he cannot rest because his brother Titus is not there with news from Corinth. So he leaves the open door and goes on to Macedonia. Then, almost in the same breath, the worry turns into thanksgiving: “But thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in triumphal procession, and through us spreads in every place the fragrance that comes from knowing him.” The picture is of a victory procession in which incense is carried, so that the scent reaches the crowds long before they see the one who is passing. Paul does not claim to be the victor. He is part of the procession, and the fragrance is Christ's. Like every scent, it cannot choose whom it reaches: “For we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing; to the one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life.” The same gospel is life to one who welcomes it and a sharp reproach to one who closes the door. Paul himself trembles at this: “Who is sufficient for these things?”

He answers by describing the kind of messenger God can use: “For we are not peddlers of God's word like so many; but in Christ we speak as persons of sincerity, as persons sent from God and standing in his presence.” A peddler waters down his goods to please the buyer. A person sent from God speaks as one who stands before God. In the Kerala monsoon, when rain has soaked the house and the cupboards smell of damp, an old household remedy is to burn a little frankincense or sambrani on a few embers. The smell fills the rooms, clings to clothes and stays in the hair. We carry with us the fragrance of whoever we have spent time with. The disciple who has stood in the presence of Christ in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono carries something of him into the market, the office and the kitchen without having to say a word.

The Gospel shows us the Lord himself in the synagogue of Nazareth, “as was his custom,” on the sabbath. The scroll of Isaiah is given to him, and he finds the place: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor.” The very word Christ means the Anointed One. The Spirit rests on him not for his own comfort but for the sake of the poor, the captive, the blind and the oppressed. Luke tells us that he then says: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The good news is not an idea about the future; it begins to happen when he opens his mouth. Paul's fragrance and the Lord's anointing are one thing seen from two sides: Christ is anointed, and the fragrance of that anointing is spread through those who belong to him.

Today the Panchangam also remembers St Alexius of Rome. The old Life of Alexius, whose historical details cannot be confirmed and which is best read as a story told by the Church to praise a way of life, tells of the only son of a wealthy Roman family who left his home and bride, lived for years as a beggar in a far-off city, and finally returned unrecognised to his father's house, where he lived out his days among the poor at the door. Whatever the details, the Church has loved this story because it makes Christ's own path visible: he who was rich became poor for our sake. Alexius's name is also borne today by Most Rev. Yoohanon Mar Alexios, whose name day the Panchangam keeps, and the Church remembers with thanks the anniversary of the episcopal ordination of Most Rev. Thomas Mar Koorilos in 1997. A bishop is anointed so that he may be a person “sent from God and standing in his presence.” We pray that these pastors, and all who serve us, may spread the fragrance of Christ.
outline: Ask: when people have been with me, what do they carry away: worry, or the fragrance of Christ?
Paul is not the victor; he carries the incense of the victory of Christ.
Point 2 · Sent from God, standing before him
A messenger is not a peddler; he speaks with sincerity from the presence of God.
The Spirit is given for the poor, the captive, the blind and the oppressed.
Point 4 · From riches to the door
St Alexius, according to the old Life, makes visible the Lord who became poor; pastors remembered today.
“Thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in triumphal procession.”
live: Before you leave home this morning, stand for one minute in prayer, and ask that whoever you meet today may meet the kindness of Christ in you.
Choose one conversation this week in which you have been tempted to soften the truth to please, and speak it gently and plainly.
Pray today by name for your bishop and your parish priest, and for Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios in particular, that they may bring good news to the poor.
2027-07-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, anointed by the Father with the Holy Spirit to bring good news to the poor, we thank you that in you we are always led in triumph. Let the fragrance of your knowledge spread through us in every place, in our homes, our work and our parish. Keep us sincere, as persons sent from God and standing in his presence, and make us gentle with the poor, the captive and the oppressed. Through the prayers of St Alexius, who for your sake became poor, and of all your saints, bless our bishops and priests, and bless Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios whom we remember today. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the incense rises before the altar, a sign of prayer and of the fragrance of Christ's sacrifice; and the priest, anointed to serve, offers on our behalf the bread and wine that become the Body and Blood of the Lord.
conn: Psalm 141:2: “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you”; Ephesians 5:2: Christ “gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.”
Isaiah 61:1–2, the passage the Lord reads at Nazareth; Acts 10:38: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and he went about doing good.
2 Corinthians 8:9: “though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.”
fathers: The fragrance of a perfume is felt by those near it even when the one who carries it says nothing; in this way the apostles, wherever they went, spread the knowledge of Christ simply by what they were (Homilies on Second Corinthians, in substance).
Christ is called the Anointed because as man he received the Spirit for our sake, so that the gift of the Spirit might pass from him to all of us who are his body (Commentary on Luke, in substance).
magis: The word Christ comes from the Greek translation of the Hebrew Messiah, which means anointed; Jesus is the Christ because he is consecrated by the Spirit as priest, prophet and king (in substance).
The kingdom belongs to the poor and the lowly, which means those who have accepted it with humble hearts; Jesus is sent to preach good news to the poor (in substance).
Love for the poor is incompatible with immoderate love of riches or their selfish use (in substance).

quick: Paul thanks God, who in Christ leads us in triumph and spreads through us the fragrance of the knowledge of Christ.
In the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus reads Isaiah: the Spirit of the Lord is upon him to bring good news to the poor.
The Panchangam remembers St Alexius of Rome, the Anointed One's way of poverty, and prays for two bishops, Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios.
2027-07-17.action: Do one hidden kindness today for someone poor or lonely, and tell no one.
2027-07-17.question: What do people carry away from me: worry, or the fragrance of Christ?

family.explain: When incense or a sweet flower is near us, we smell it even without being told. St Paul says that people who stay close to Jesus smell like Jesus: kind, gentle and glad. The Holy Spirit was given to Jesus so that he could bring good news to the poor, and he gives us the same Spirit so that we can share his kindness. The Church today remembers St Alexius, who in an old story left a rich home to live among the poor.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, and for families who are poor.
family.ask: Ask: “How can I be the fragrance of Jesus at home today?”

illus: In the rains of Karkidakam, a grandmother in a Kottayam house lit a little sambrani on a bit of charcoal in an old coconut shell each evening. The smoke drifted through every room, past the beds and the prayer corner, and her grandchildren said they could tell which house was theirs by the smell on their school bags. One evening a visiting cousin laughed and asked why she bothered, since the damp always came back by morning. She answered that the damp came back, yes, but so did she, and a house is not made clean in one evening. Years later, the cousin said that her own children, when they smelled sambrani on a wet evening, said at once, “This is Ammachi.” The grandmother was never preaching, but the whole house said where she had been and who she belonged to.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, anointed by the Spirit to bring good news to the poor, let us be your fragrance in our homes and parish. Amen.
share: Thanks be to God, who spreads through us the fragrance that comes from knowing him (2 Corinthians 2:14). What do people smell on me?
We are persons sent from God and standing in his presence (2 Corinthians 2:17). Do I speak from his presence or to please people?
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor (Luke 4:18). Who is the poor person God puts in my way?
pm.resp: Lord, let us be your fragrance.
interc: For Most Rev. Thomas Mar Koorilos, on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination, and for Most Rev. Yoohanon Mar Alexios on his name day, that they may serve with joy.
For our bishops, priests and deacons, that they may be sincere ministers of the word of God.
For the poor, the homeless and the lonely, that they may meet the good news in our kindness.
For families in this rainy season, for the sick and for those with damp, crowded homes.
For all who have left comfort for the sake of the gospel, that they may be sustained.

term: The word Christ is the Greek translation of the Hebrew Mashiach, which means one who has been anointed with oil. Kings, priests and prophets of Israel were anointed. Jesus is the Anointed One in a unique way, because he is anointed by the Holy Spirit himself.
kidsaint: Long ago, so the story goes, a young man of Rome named Alexius was very rich. But he wanted to love God more than he loved gold. So he gave up his comfortable life and lived among poor people. After many years he came back to his father's house, but nobody knew him, so he lived quietly under the stairs and was kind to everyone. Lesson: Jesus became poor so that we might become rich, and those who follow him can learn to love people more than things. (This is an old story, and we cannot be sure about its details.)

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul says something beautiful: thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in triumph, and through us spreads in every place the fragrance that comes from knowing him (2 Corinthians 2:14). The picture is of a procession in which incense is carried, so that its scent reaches people before they even see the one who is passing. Paul is not the victor; Christ is. But Paul and all of us who belong to Christ carry his fragrance.

In these monsoon days, many of our homes use a little incense to drive away the damp smell. The smell stays in our clothes and hair for hours. Paul says it is like this with the gospel: those who have been with Christ carry something of him wherever they go. He adds: we are not peddlers of God's word like so many, but in Christ we speak as persons of sincerity, as persons sent from God and standing in his presence (2 Corinthians 2:17). Let us not water down the gospel to please people.

In the Gospel, Jesus stands up in the synagogue of Nazareth and reads from Isaiah: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor (Luke 4:18). The Anointed One is anointed for the poor, the captive, the blind and the oppressed. That is the fragrance we are to spread. Today the Church remembers St Alexius of Rome, who, according to the old story, left his riches to live among the poor, and she prays for Thomas Mar Koorilos on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination and for Yoohanon Mar Alexios on his name day.
Let us ask the Lord to make us people who carry the fragrance of Christ: in our kindness to the poor, in our honesty, in the way we pray and the way we speak. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever smelled incense in the church, or a sweet flower in the garden? You can smell it even if you cannot see it! St Paul says that people who stay close to Jesus carry something sweet with them, the love of Jesus. When you are kind to your friends, when you share with someone poor, when you say sorry, people can tell that you belong to Jesus. Today, try to carry the sweet smell of Jesus to everyone you meet.

sub: The old Life of St Alexius.
He who was rich became poor.
q: Happy are those who consider the poor; the Lord delivers them in the day of trouble.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Pray by name for Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios and for your own pastors.

concl: The gospel spreads like fragrance through people who have stood in Christ's presence.
The Anointed One is sent to the poor, and so are those who are his.
2027-07-17.resolve: Carry the fragrance of Christ, speak with sincerity, and bring good news to the poor.
